items.title: Thai teenager's father 'deeply saddened' over her death as Australian man charged with murder
items.description: The family of a 17-year-old girl in Thailand speak of their grief as an Australian man is charged with her murder.

items.title: Major capital cities record worst housing auction clearance rates in years
items.description: Sydney and Melbourne record their weakest auction results in years, with fewer than half of all homes going under the hammer finding a buyer.

items.title: Treasurer promises to 'fix' property tax oversight, but won't say how exactly
items.description: The Treasurer is promising to "fix" an unintended consequence of the government's overhaul of property tax breaks to protect widows and divorcees — but he has refused to say exactly how.

items.title: US strikes Iran, Iran hits Bahrain and Kuwait as Middle East tensions escalate
items.description: The United States and Iran have exchanged strikes against targets in the Middle East, underscoring rising tensions that threaten the interim deal between the two nations to stop the war.

items.title: England captain Ben Stokes announces retirement during Test match
items.description: England captain Ben Stokes will retire from international cricket after the third Test against New Zealand, the team has said.

items.title: What happened when the ABC went to uncover Bali's 'Island of Trash'
items.description: Known to many as the Island of the Gods, residents fear Bali may soon become the "Island of Trash" due to a deluge of tourists, a lack of rubbish education and the partial closure of a much-needed landfill facility.

items.title: Australian run of Waitress closing early with Sydney shows cancelled
items.description: The Australian stage production of Waitress will no longer continue on its national tour, with planned shows in Sydney now cancelled.

items.title: Skydiving plane crashes in France, killing all 11 people on board
items.description: A small aircraft carrying skydivers has crashed in eastern France, killing all 11 people on board, local authorities say.

items.title: Footy's quiet crisis claims its youngest victim
items.description: A talent and a team player, Nick Lowden excelled at Aussie Rules. But the knocks, bumps, hits and collisions were adding up.

items.title: Piastri has 'really good day', Russell survives late charge in Austria
items.description: Oscar Piastri has hailed his fourth place at Sunday's Austrian Grand Prix as a "really good day", while Mercedes George Russell held on to claim his first victory since the start of the season.

items.title: Blues ring in the changes as To'o dumped for decider
items.description: New South Wales coach Laurie Daley has made five changes to the Blues side for Origin III with Brian To'o missing out for the first time in over five years.

items.title: Photos capture highs, lows and quirks of World Cup football fandom
items.description: From donning face paint to viral chants, each fandom has its peculiarities.

items.title: If the UK has become ungovernable, some people say Brexit is to blame
items.description: It took only a month after coming to office for Keir Starmer's popularity to begin plummeting. Does it mean the UK has become ungovernable? Or is something else to blame?

items.title: Hanson spawned the silliest semantic beard-stroking in 20 years
items.description: We've come a long way since it was Pauline Hanson who didn't know the meaning of big words.

items.title: Meta won't memorialise Facebook account five years after man's death
items.description: After Marija Milisavljević's husband died in 2021, she wanted to memorialise his Facebook account to keep a trove of photos and videos, but tech giant Meta has not made it easy.

items.title: Keith Urban is a country megastar — so why release a yacht rock album?
items.description: Keith Urban explains why he made a yacht rock album and how his Brisbane cover band days shaped Flow State.

items.title: Love story: My dad is Blues legend Steve Mortimer. I'm grieving him in real time
items.description: Erin Mortimer's dad, Bulldogs and Blues legend Steve Mortimer, was diagnosed with dementia at just 60 after years of concussions during his playing career. Erin is holding on to the special memories, and the glimmers of him that remain.

items.title: How many products in your daily life are made from fossil fuels?
items.description: Coal, oil and gas are major ingredients for far more than just energy. Why are we so reliant on oil, and how difficult would it be to find other resources?

items.title: Family still reeling after death of baby in regional WA
items.description: The parents of Willow Horne are still looking for answers after the eight-month-old died in a regional WA hospital.

items.title: Karl Stefanovic's 'weird personality' might score him a Logie
items.description: Karl Stefanovic is no longer part of the Nine family but his audience may not be ready to abandon their prodigal son.

items.title: The artefacts that tell the story of one of Australia's most notorious cases
items.description: Forty years ago, the chance discovery of a bloodied matinee jacket unravelled a murder conviction. Now, that evidence lives inside a national museum's collection that's too sensitive for public display.

items.title: Trump's Vance jokes fuel succession speculation
items.description: At times, Donald Trump appears to be harking back to his days hosting reality TV show The Apprentice as he leans into speculation about who he will anoint as his successor.

items.title: Thousands still missing after Venezuela earthquakes as death toll passes 1,400
items.description: The death toll from two earthquakes in Venezuela has climbed beyond 1,400, as searches for survivors intensify during the remaining hours of the window for survival.

items.title: Singha beer dynasty being torn apart by 'ungrateful child' law
items.description: The billionaire family behind the Singha beer company is being torn apart by explosive allegations of assault and a century-old law that protects parents from neglectful children.

items.title: 'Worst' wind lull pushes green poster child South Australia to its power limits
items.description: South Australia is at the bleeding edge of the energy transition but record low winds have pushed its grid to the brink of its limits.
